note: Singing-modes step 1: Dorian over a drone, built from the minor pentatonic (the 2nd and the 6th added), then a made-up tune over the Dorian vamp that lands on the 6th as {{chord:IV7}} comes round; the vamp's chords are tokens counted the long way. Key and tempo are moves (70 up to 90) in place of the old Key selector, with a {{?key}} line.

exercise.title: Dorian over a drone
exercise.why: Over a drone you hear every note of a mode against its home note, and Dorian is the minor pentatonic scale with two notes added, so sing the five notes first and then add the two new ones.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff. These are the five notes of the minor pentatonic scale on {{1}}. Sing them from the low {{1}} up to the next {{1}} and back down. Sing them on "oo".
Practice until each note settles against the drone without a slide.

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff. The two ringed notes, {{2}} and {{6}}, turn the pentatonic scale into Dorian. Sing the whole scale from the low {{1}} up to the next {{1}} and back down. Sing it on "oo".
Then sing {{5}}, {{6}}, {{b7}} and up to {{1}}, slowly. Practice until {{6}} lands without a slide.
{{?key}}In another key the drone moves, and {{6}} is still a whole step above {{5}}.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together, at {{=bpm}}. The backing track plays {{chord:i7}} and {{chord:IV7}} in turn.
{{chord:i7}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, and {{chord:IV7}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}. Make up a short tune from the scale, and land on {{6}} when {{chord:IV7}} comes round: it is the 3rd of that chord. Sing it on "la".
If you lose your place, hold {{1}} until {{chord:i7}} comes back.
